notes: [COUNSEL] Card has no sentence on distillation; MIT has no output restriction on its face. A provenance question remains for any open model trained on another vendor's outputs. Secondary sources report Kimi K3 has a custom licence; not checked.

value: A model is anonymous only if extraction and query-based retrieval of training personal data are both insignificantly likely; assess case by case
conditions: Applies to models trained on personal data; EU GDPR
quote: the likelihood of obtaining, intentionally or not, such personal data from queries, should be insignificant
notes: [COUNSEL] Default stance: thorough evaluation needed. An adapter trained on personal data should be presumed to contain personal data until shown otherwise, so deletion, DSR and transfer duties may attach to adapter weights.

value: Legitimate interest is available but only on a documented three-step test; no hierarchy of bases
conditions: Development and deployment of AI models; Art. 21 objection right applies
quote: (1) identifying the legitimate interest pursued by the controller or a third party; (2) analysing the necessity of the processing
notes: [COUNSEL] Step 3 is the balancing test. Public availability is only one factor in reasonable expectations; the Opinion lists it alongside the data subject relationship and source. Web scraping is flagged as a significant-impact risk.

value: Unlawful training can taint later processing unless the model is demonstrably anonymised
conditions: Scenario 3; Scenarios 1 and 2 cover retained personal data, including a later controller's own assessment
quote: Hence, the unlawfulness of the initial processing should not impact the subsequent operation of the model.
notes: [COUNSEL] Quote applies only where subsequent operation does not process personal data. Otherwise SAs may intervene, and brands deploying a model could have to assess its origin. A contaminated shared base spreads risk to every tenant.

value: Respect robots.txt or ai.txt, exclude sensitive sources, offer an opt-out list
conditions: Examples, non-exhaustive, assessed case by case
quote: by respecting robots.txt or ai.txt files or any other recognised mechanism to express exclusion from automated crawling or scraping
notes: [COUNSEL] GDPR mitigations do not cure a contract breach under platform terms. Both layers must be passed.

value: A processor acts only on documented instructions; one that determines purposes and means is treated as a controller for that processing
conditions: Art. 28(3)(a) and 28(10); training a brand's adapter on its instructions versus training Synquic's own base
quote: the processor shall be considered to be a controller in respect of that processing.
notes: [COUNSEL] gdpr-info.eu is an unofficial mirror of the Regulation; EUR-Lex returned empty pages to the fetcher. Working position: per-brand adapter on instruction points to processor; pooling brand personal data into a shared base points to controller with its own lawful basis and notice.

value: Reusing customer data to build a new AI system makes the reuser responsible for that new processing
conditions: French regulator guidance; streaming-platform example; published 07 June 2024
quote: reuses a dataset of its customers that was originally collected for the purpose of providing the service.
notes: [COUNSEL] A CNIL checklist adds a compatibility test for reuse unless consent, law or research applies, and informs data subjects in advance. National guidance, not binding across the EU.

value: Art. 22 bars decisions based solely on automated processing with legal or similarly significant effects; Art. 35 requires a DPIA for likely high-risk processing, notably new technologies and systematic extensive evaluation
quote: not to be subject to a decision based solely on automated processing,
notes: [COUNSEL] Content generation alone is unlikely to be an Art. 22 decision; audience targeting or eligibility-style use could differ. Plan a DPIA for any training on personal data; CNIL recommends one for AI development. Art. 35 fetched at gdpr-info.eu/art-35-gdpr/. Unofficial mirror.

notes: [COUNSEL] Council text not read. Sources differ on numbering and form: Article 88c (Commission), Article 88bis presumption (Irish Presidency draft), recital 33a (this source). Document numbers also differ (13886/26 vs 14756/26). Planning must use current Art. 6 until adopted; early 2027 is reported as the earliest conclusion.

notes: [COUNSEL] More permissive than the GDPR processor position and than platform terms. Whether a shared base that embeds personal information crosses the 'another person' line is untested in these materials. Do not build on California's rule alone.

value: Personal information formats include AI systems capable of outputting personal information

quote: artificial intelligence systems that are capable of outputting personal information.
notes: [COUNSEL] Parallels the EDPB anonymity view. Adapter weights able to emit personal information could be in scope for access and deletion.

value: Risk assessment required when processing to train ADMT for a significant decision, or facial, emotion or identity-related technology

quote: Processing the personal information of consumers, which the business intends to use to train an ADMT for a significant decision concerning a consumer;
notes: [COUNSEL] Social content generation is unlikely to be a significant decision. The video engine could trigger the facial or identity limb if it trains on faces for identification or emotion recognition. Staggered dates are from secondary sources.

value: Act does not apply to personal data made publicly available by the Data Principal or under a legal duty

notes: [COUNSEL] Illustration in the Act uses a blogger on social media. Scope for third-party reposts is untested. It lifts DPDP only, not platform terms. Substantive duties are reportedly not yet in force (R7-051).

conditions: Rule 4 Consent Manager registration; conflicts with 2026-11-14 in R7-051
notes: Read through search index; direct fetch of this site returned 503. Same source says no Data Protection Board appointment was notified as at 9 September 2026.

notes: [COUNSEL] Commission FAQ (R7-054) gives the same date. If the video engine launches now it is in the no-grace group, so marking must ship with launch. Substantial changes to an older system may also matter.

Omnibus reported as Regulation (EU) 2026/1744, in force 2026-07-27; EUR-Lex text returned empty to the fetcher, so the number is confirmed only through search index entries from EUR-Lex and OEIL.

entity: EU AI Act Art. 5 as amended

quote: transparency obligations for providers and deployers pursuant to Article 50

entity: Commission Guidelines on Art. 50, C(2026) 5054 final
value: A company that modifies another provider's generative system with new training data and offers it under its own name becomes provider of the new system
conditions: Art. 50 transparency roles; adopted 2026-07-20; Art. 3(3) own name or trademark test
quote: modifies that system (e.g. with new training data)
notes: [COUNSEL] Key correction to the brief's framing: Synquic is a provider of an AI system for Art. 50(1)-(2) even if it never becomes a GPAI model provider. Providers are in scope wherever located if output is used in the Union. Guidelines are non-binding.

entity: Commission Guidelines on Art. 50, C(2026) 5054 final
value: Deep fake covers simulated subjects that could plausibly exist, not only real identifiable people
conditions: Paragraph on 'existing' in section 6.1.1; realistic output that would falsely appear authentic
quote: to resemble someone or something that exists, can plausibly exist or could have plausibly existed in reality to be considered a deep fake
notes: [COUNSEL] Trap: 'it is a made-up person' is not an exit from Art. 50(4) labelling. Listed deep fake examples include a realistic CEO avatar and a product image that misleads as to appearance. A non-deepfake example is mice arguing about cheese in a cheese advert.

entity: Commission Guidelines on Art. 50, C(2026) 5054 final
value: Advertising deep fakes usually do not get the lighter artistic or creative regime; a realistic synthetic influencer testing a sponsored real product is a listed non-exempt example
conditions: Art. 50(4) artistic exception; case-specific
quote: AI-manipulated video featuring a realistic synthetic influencer testing out a sponsored real product, focused solely on displaying the product functionalities.
notes: [COUNSEL] Guidelines say some advertisements might be evidently creative in specific situations; content that is exclusively commercial and recognisable as such is excluded.

entity: Commission Guidelines on Art. 50, C(2026) 5054 final
value: A company merely commissioning an agency, without control over AI use, is not a deployer; the party using the system under its authority is
conditions: Paragraphs 14 and 15; a party can be provider and deployer together
quote: without taking decision s and exercising control over whether and how the advertising agency uses AI in the production process, is not a deployer.
notes: [COUNSEL] 'decision s' reproduces a PDF spacing artefact. If Synquic operates the engine and delivers finished video, Synquic itself can be the deployer owing the label. If brands self-serve, they are. DPAs should allocate this.

entity: Commission Guidelines on Art. 50, C(2026) 5054 final
value: Intermediate outputs in closed-loop production workflows need no marking; final outputs from workflow stages do
conditions: Art. 50(2); examples include film, animation, games or advertising production
quote: In those cases, only the final output from workflow stages has to be marked and detectable.
notes: [COUNSEL] Implies the render pipeline should mark at export, and must survive transcoding to stay detectable.

entity: Code of Practice on marking and labelling AI-generated content
value: Final published 2026-06-10; voluntary; Section 1 providers, Section 2 deployers
conditions: Assessed adequate by Commission and AI Board per Commission FAQ; read through search index
quote: Signing the code of practice is voluntary. Not signing it does not constitute non-compliance with the AI Act.
notes: [COUNSEL] Publication date is from press release IP/26/1328. Code text itself was not read, so required techniques (watermark plus metadata) are not confirmed here.

value: Downstream modifier becomes GPAI provider when modification training compute is greater than a third of the original model's training compute
conditions: Indicative criterion, paragraph 60; forward-looking, few modifications expected to meet it (paragraph 64)
quote: the training compute used for the modification is greater than a third of the training compute of the original model
notes: [COUNSEL] Guidelines are non-binding. Paragraph 115 counts compute directly contributing to parameter updates for non-systemic models; whether separate per-brand adapters aggregate is not addressed in the passages read. Page lists publication 2025-07-18 and last update 2026-04-20.

value: If original compute is unknown: a third of 10^25 FLOP for a systemic-risk model, otherwise a third of 10^23 FLOP
conditions: Paragraph 61; applies when the modifier cannot know or estimate the value
quote: it should be replaced with a third of the threshold that is part of the indicative criterion
notes: [COUNSEL] Log FLOP per training run from day one so Synquic can evidence that it stays under the line.

value: Training compute greater than 10^23 FLOP and able to generate language, text-to-image or text-to-video
conditions: Paragraph 17; relevant if Synquic trains its own shared base or video model from scratch
quote: its training compute is greater than 1023 FLOP and it can generate language (whether in the form of text3 or audio4), text-to-image, or text-to-video.
notes: [COUNSEL] '1023' is 10^23 and text3, audio4 carry footnote marks from PDF extraction. A base trained above this line is a GPAI model and Synquic is its provider: Art. 53 duties include a public training-content summary and copyright policy. Modifier duties, by contrast, are limited to the modification and its data (paragraph 65).

entity: FTC Consumer Reviews and Testimonials Rule, 16 CFR 465
value: No blanket ban on AI avatars in marketing; fake testimonials and unauthorised celebrity avatars implying endorsement violate the rule
conditions: Rule effective 2024-10-21; courts may impose civil penalties for knowing violations
quote: The rule has no blanket prohibition on the use of AI-generated avatars in marketing.
notes: [COUNSEL] FTC Act Section 5 deception can still apply. No general federal AI-content label duty was found. A synthetic person giving a 'customer' testimonial is the high-risk pattern.

value: Final order set aside 2025-12-22; FTC found the order unduly burdens innovation and the complaint facts did not support Section 5
conditions: AI writing tool that could generate reviews
quote: because the order unduly burdens innovation in the nascent AI industry, it is in the public interest to set it aside.
notes: [COUNSEL] Lowers federal means-and-instrumentalities risk for tool makers for now, not for advertisers. Enforcement stance can change with the Commission.

value: Conspicuous disclosure required in ads containing a synthetic performer, where the creator has actual knowledge; effective about 2026-06-09
conditions: Commercial ads in any medium; audio ads, translation of a human performer and consistent promotion of expressive works exempt; media outlets exempt
quote: a human performer who is not recognizable as any identifiable natural performer.
notes: [COUNSEL] Trap: the fetch tool's summary said non-recognizable performers are excluded; the statute text says the reverse, the definition targets them. Civil penalty 1000 USD first violation, 5000 USD subsequent. Effective 180th day after signing on 2025-12-11; June 9 2026 reported by law firms. Federal EO 14365 targets state AI laws; no suit against this law was found, and that search only ran to April 2026.

conditions: Provider disclosures and detection tool
